_comment: The accent themes the console offers. This file is the ONE source: the picker
reads it, and scripts/gen-accents.mjs turns it into assets/accents.css. Edit
here and run `npm run gen:accents` — it also runs before every build, so the
shipped stylesheet cannot drift from this file.
Steps 500 and up are pulled one step darker than the usual Tailwind ramp for the
warm accents. At their normal weight, orange-500 and lime-500 carry a focus ring
on white at under 3:1 and white button text at under 4.5:1 — legible on the dark
theme and not on the light one. accents.spec.ts is what found that.
nearState declares that an accent sits within 25° of a state colour. Orange is
17° from warning and is shipped deliberately; it stays tellable apart because it
is materially deeper than warning-500, and because the console conveys state with
an icon and a word as well as a colour.
The declaration is not a mute button: the test checks it names the state the
accent is ACTUALLY nearest, so it cannot go stale, and an undeclared collision
still fails.
Green and red were asked for and dropped: both land at 0° — green-500 IS
success-500 and red-500 IS danger-500. An accent indistinguishable from 'this
went wrong' makes every primary button read as a warning.
Teal was tried and dropped: teal-600 carries white button text at only 3.74:1.
dark50 is the only step a dark theme overrides: the -50 tint has to darken rather
than lighten, while steps 100-900 read correctly on both grounds.
